newsitem.title: USA: Controversial rap duo leave Disney after album recall.
newsitem.headline: Controversial rap duo leave Disney after album recall.

text.p: The Detroit rap duo whose lewd album was pulled from stores last month by a nervous Walt Disney Co., have resurfaced at a new label, a spokeswoman for the musicians said Wednesday.

Insane Clown Posse had been signed to Disney's Hollywood Records. But when Disney executives learned of the content of their hotly-anticipated label debut "The Great Milenko," they ordered a recall six hours after it went on sale on June 24.

The unprecedented action did not stop the album from selling 18,000 copies and debuting at 63 on the Billboard 200 album charts, making Insane Clown Posse the only successful new act in Hollywood's eight-year history. In its third week of release, the album still managed to sell about 9,700 copies, indicating that some retailers ignored Disney's order.
Insane Clown Posse consists of Violent J. and Shaggy 2 Dope, two face paint-wearing white rappers otherwise known as Joe Bruce and Joe Utsler, respectively.

Disney said the album was "inappropriate," and both sides entered talks to release the band from its contract. Island Records, whose roster includes U2 and the Cranberries, emerged as Insane Clown Posse's new home, their spokeswoman said.

It is not known what songs unnerved Disney. But the company, and the music industry in general, has come under pressure from conservative groups. Southern Baptists last month launched a boycott of Disney products in response to what they consider Disney's liberal attitude towards gays.

One of "Milenko's" songs, "Hallelujah" skewers religious zealots who pump money from their congregations, while another "Hall of Illusions," advocates death for spousal abusers. Another track features a suicide hotline counselor who threatens to blow a "nerdy bitch" caller's brains out.

Island, which is owned by Dutch media giant PolyGram NV, will re-release "The Great Milenko" in mid-August, with three songs that the group had reluctantly withdrawn from "Milenko" at Hollywood's request, the spokeswoman said.
Island and Hollywood officials were not available for comment.
